Issue #4: toc: let me exclude a heading from the table of contents Some of our pages have headings that shouldn't be in the table of contents (for example a "Contents" heading right above the `[TOC]` marker, or "Edit this page" footers), but they still need to be real headings with an id so people can link to them. There's no way to do this today. I'd like to mark such a heading with a class, using `attr_list`: ```markdown # Guide ## Contents {: .no-toc } [TOC] ## Install ## Usage ``` With the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions, the TOC should list "Guide", "Install" and "Usage" but not "Contents". The "Contents" heading itself should still be rendered with its id (`id="contents"`) so anchors keep working. The same should apply to `md.toc_tokens`, since our theme builds its sidebar from it. `no-toc` as the class name would be great (it's what our old static site generator used), but I don't mind if it's configurable. input.summary: The PR strips entries from the rendered `[TOC]` HTML with a regex postprocessor. That fixes the issue's example only. `md.toc_tokens` and `md.toc` still list the excluded heading, which the issue explicitly asks to change. The regex also gives wrong output for nested and similarly named classes. The fix belongs in `TocTreeprocessor`, before the tokens and the TOC HTML are built.

findings.title: md.toc_tokens and md.toc still include no-toc headings
findings.evidence:
Running `Markdown(extensions=['toc','attr_list'])` on the issue's example, `md.toc_tokens` still contains {'id':'contents',...} as a child of Guide. `md.toc` still contains `
  • Contents
    • `. Only the `[TOC]` placeholder output in the body was changed, by a postprocessor that edits the final HTML. The issue says the exclusion must also apply to `md.toc_tokens`. The filtering needs to happen in TocTreeprocessor when the toc tokens are collected.

findings.title: Regex postprocessor is wrong for nesting and class matching
findings.evidence:
Input `[TOC]

# A
## B {: .foo .no-toc }
## C {: .no-toc-x }` rendered a TOC with both B and C removed and an empty `<ul>` left behind. C's class is only `no-toc-x`, but `class="[^"]*no-toc[^"]*"` is a substring match. Input `# A
## Sub {: .no-toc }
### Deep
## B` produced a malformed nested `<ul><ul>` structure with Sub's child orphaned. The regex also assumes `class` comes before `id` in the heading tag.

findings.title: Test only covers the rendered-HTML case
findings.evidence: The single new test only checks two `assertIn`/`assertNotIn` substrings in the HTML output. It does not check `md.toc_tokens` or `md.toc`. It does not check that the heading keeps `id="contents"`. It does not check nested headings or a class that merely contains `no-toc`.

notes: The existing suite passes (1167 tests, OK), but none of those tests exercise the new behaviour.
The issue allows the class name to be configurable. The PR hard-codes `no-toc`, which is acceptable, but a config option would be nicer.
